name: Mount Everest
intro: The world's highest mountain rises above the Khumbu region on the Nepal–China border.
description: Everest stands in the high Himalaya, where immense glaciers and sharply cut ridges shape a landscape shared by Nepal and Tibet. The southern approach passes through Sherpa communities and Sagarmatha National Park; the northern route begins on the Tibetan Plateau.
history: Known as Sagarmatha in Nepal and Chomolungma in Tibet, the mountain has long held deep cultural meaning for people of the region. The 1953 expedition of Tenzing Norgay and Edmund Hillary made the first confirmed ascent. Today, climbing is tightly shaped by permits, weather windows and the expertise of local high-altitude teams.
geography: Everest is part of the Khumbu Himal and is built from uplifted sedimentary and metamorphic rock. Its summit ridge forms the international boundary; the Khumbu Icefall and Western Cwm define the classic southern route.
climbing: A summit attempt is an extreme high-altitude expedition requiring extensive acclimatization, technical preparation, permits and experienced professional support. Lower Khumbu trails offer rewarding trekking without a summit attempt.
facts: Official elevation: 8,848.86 m, jointly announced by Nepal and China in 2020.
The mountain is named Sagarmatha in Nepal and Chomolungma in Tibet.
The Khumbu region is home to Sherpa communities and the UNESCO-listed Sagarmatha National Park.

name: K2
intro: The world's second-highest summit is an unmistakable pyramid in the remote Karakoram.
description: K2 rises above the Baltoro Glacier in a vast landscape of granite spires, ice and high mountain passes. Its steep faces and rapidly changing weather have earned it a formidable reputation among climbers.
history: The peak was surveyed in 1856 and marked K2 in the Great Trigonometrical Survey of India. Italian climbers Lino Lacedelli and Achille Compagnoni reached the summit in 1954. The mountain and its approaches remain inseparable from the knowledge and work of Balti communities and high-altitude teams.
geography: K2 lies in the Baltoro Muztagh subrange of the Karakoram, near the Pakistan–China boundary. Its summit is a steep, exposed pyramid surrounded by major glaciers.
climbing: The trek to K2 Base Camp is a demanding, remote journey over glacial terrain. Climbing the mountain is an advanced expedition requiring technical skills, acclimatization, permits and professional support.
facts: At 8,611 m, K2 is the world's second-highest mountain.
Its name records its survey designation: the second peak measured in the Karakoram.
The Abruzzi Spur is the most commonly climbed route, but remains highly technical.

name: Kangchenjunga
intro: A vast five-summit massif revered in the eastern Himalaya.
description: Kangchenjunga stands on the Nepal–India border and dominates the remote valleys of eastern Nepal and Sikkim. Its glaciers, forests and exceptional biodiversity make the surrounding landscape as remarkable as the summit.
history: The name is commonly interpreted from Tibetan as 'the five treasures of the high snow.' The first ascent was made in 1955 by Joe Brown and George Band, who stopped just short of the summit in respect for a local promise. That tradition has been observed by many subsequent teams.
geography: The massif sits in the Kangchenjunga Himal, a section of the eastern Himalaya. Protected landscapes on both sides of the border conserve important habitats and high-altitude ecosystems.
climbing: Expeditions are remote and logistically demanding. Treks in the region require careful planning, local permissions and respect for protected areas and local customs.
facts: At 8,586 m, it is the world's third-highest mountain.
The name refers to five high peaks or 'treasures of the snow.'
The first ascent team deliberately left the summit untouched in respect for local tradition.

name: Lhotse
intro: A towering Himalayan neighbor of Everest, joined to it by the South Col.
description: Lhotse's main summit forms part of the same high ridge as Everest. Its south face is one of the largest and steepest mountain faces in the world, rising above the Khumbu and Imja valleys.
history: The first ascent of Lhotse was completed in 1956 by a Swiss team led by Ernst Reiss and Fritz Luchsinger. Though often overshadowed by Everest, Lhotse has a distinct climbing history and a celebrated reputation for technical difficulty.
geography: Lhotse is the fourth-highest mountain on Earth. Its name means 'South Peak' in Tibetan, reflecting its position south of Everest along the shared massif.
climbing: The standard route shares the upper approach with Everest and is an extreme expedition. The south face is reserved for highly experienced alpinists.
facts: Lhotse is the fourth-highest mountain at 8,516 m.
It is connected to Everest by the South Col.
Lhotse Middle, at 8,414 m, was long regarded as one of the highest unclimbed named points.

name: Makalu
intro: A sharply isolated pyramid whose four ridges rise above the eastern Himalaya.
description: Makalu's steep faces and knife-edge ridges create one of the most striking profiles in Nepal. It lies within Makalu Barun National Park, a protected area spanning subtropical forest through alpine terrain.
history: The first ascent was made in 1955 by a French expedition led by Jean Franco. The team reached the summit in stages, an achievement that helped establish Makalu as a major objective in Himalayan mountaineering.
geography: Makalu is the world's fifth-highest mountain and is separated from Everest by the deep Kangshung Valley. The surrounding national park is renowned for its ecological range.
climbing: The normal route includes exposed ridges and steep snow and ice. The long approach and altitude demand expedition experience and thorough acclimatization.
facts: Makalu reaches 8,485 m.
Its name is thought to derive from the Sanskrit Maha-Kala.
Makalu Barun National Park protects a remarkable range of habitats around the mountain.

name: Cho Oyu
intro: A high Himalayan summit near the Nangpa La trade route between Nepal and Tibet.
description: Cho Oyu is the sixth-highest mountain on Earth and sits west of Everest. Its broad, snow-covered form rises above a region of glaciers and historic trans-Himalayan crossings.
history: An Austrian team led by Herbert Tichy, Sepp Jöchler and Pasang Dawa Lama made the first ascent in 1954. Their achievement is remembered as an early landmark in post-war Himalayan climbing.
geography: Cho Oyu stands on the Nepal–China border in the Mahalangur Himal. Nangpa La, a historic route between Tibet and the Khumbu, lies nearby.
climbing: Although often considered a more attainable 8,000-metre peak, Cho Oyu is still an extreme altitude expedition. Conditions, permits and route hazards require experienced guidance.
facts: Cho Oyu is 8,188 m high.
Its name is often translated as 'Turquoise Goddess.'
The mountain's first ascent in 1954 was among the earliest successful climbs of an 8,000-metre peak.

name: Dhaulagiri I
intro: A colossal isolated Himalayan massif west of the Kali Gandaki gorge.
description: Dhaulagiri I's long ridges and steep ice-covered walls dominate western Nepal. The mountain is set amid remote valleys and high passes, with a dramatic landscape shaped by glaciers and the Kali Gandaki river system.
history: After several challenging attempts, a Swiss-Austrian-Nepali expedition made the first ascent in 1960. A small aircraft was used to support the expedition, a notable logistical innovation for the era.
geography: At 8,167 m, Dhaulagiri I is the seventh-highest mountain in the world. The name comes from Sanskrit words meaning 'white' and 'mountain.'
climbing: The standard route crosses avalanche-prone terrain and requires expedition-level preparation. Treks around Dhaulagiri are remote and should be planned with experienced local operators.
facts: Dhaulagiri I is the highest peak of the Dhaulagiri range.
Its summit elevation is 8,167 m.
The deep Kali Gandaki gorge runs between Dhaulagiri and the Annapurna massif.

name: Manaslu
intro: The 'Mountain of the Spirit' overlooks the historic villages of Nepal's Gorkha region.
description: Manaslu is the eighth-highest mountain and the centerpiece of a landscape of glaciers, high pastures and culturally rich villages. The Manaslu Circuit brings trekkers through varied Himalayan scenery.
history: A Japanese expedition made the first ascent in 1956, led by Toshio Imanishi and Gyalzen Norbu. The mountain has since become a prominent expedition peak and the surrounding region is protected through a restricted-area permit system.
geography: Manaslu rises in the Mansiri Himal of west-central Nepal. Its long ridges connect to neighboring summits and its glaciers feed the Budhi Gandaki river.
climbing: The Manaslu Circuit is a demanding high-altitude trek with remote sections and a high pass. Climbers need expedition experience, appropriate permits and careful acclimatization.
facts: Manaslu stands at 8,163 m.
The name is derived from the Sanskrit word manasa, meaning 'intellect' or 'soul.'
The Larkya La pass on the popular circuit reaches about 5,106 m.

name: Nanga Parbat
intro: A monumental Himalayan peak above the Indus River and Pakistan's Diamer region.
description: Nanga Parbat rises dramatically from the Indus valley, with the immense Rupal Face on its southern side. It is the westernmost major 8,000-metre peak of the Himalaya and a powerful presence in Gilgit-Baltistan.
history: The Austrian climber Hermann Buhl made the first ascent in 1953, reaching the summit alone after his partners turned back. Earlier expeditions suffered serious losses, shaping the mountain's enduring reputation.
geography: Nanga Parbat means 'Naked Mountain.' Its 8,126-metre summit and enormous relief make it one of the most prominent peaks in the world.
climbing: The mountain's scale, objective hazards and unpredictable weather make climbing a serious expedition. The Fairy Meadows approach offers a celebrated view but is a remote mountain journey.
facts: Nanga Parbat is the ninth-highest mountain at 8,126 m.
The Rupal Face rises roughly 4,600 m above its base.
Hermann Buhl made the first ascent in 1953 in a landmark solo push.

name: Broad Peak
intro: A broad, multi-summited 8,000-metre peak above the upper Baltoro Glacier.
description: Broad Peak stands close to K2 and the Gasherbrum group in one of the world's great high-mountain amphitheaters. Its long summit ridge gives the mountain its name and distinguishes it from the sharper neighboring peaks.
history: A 1957 Austrian expedition led by Marcus Schmuck made the first ascent. The team climbed without supplementary oxygen, an important achievement in the early era of high-altitude mountaineering.
geography: Broad Peak is the twelfth-highest mountain on Earth and lies along the Pakistan–China frontier. Its massif has several distinct high points along a lengthy crest.
climbing: The approach shares the demanding Baltoro Glacier trek. The upper mountain is exposed and conditions can change quickly; a climb requires experienced expedition planning.
facts: Broad Peak rises to 8,051 m.
It is less than 10 km from K2.
The summit ridge extends for more than a kilometre and contains multiple high points.

name: Gasherbrum I
intro: Known as Hidden Peak, this remote 8,000-metre summit is deep in the Karakoram.
description: Gasherbrum I rises in the Gasherbrum group above the upper Baltoro region. Its remote setting, glaciated approaches and complex ridges make it a formidable objective far from settled valleys.
history: An American expedition led by Nicholas Clinch made the first ascent in 1958. The mountain's nickname, Hidden Peak, reflects how it is screened from many viewpoints along the main Karakoram trekking route.
geography: Gasherbrum I lies on the Pakistan–China border and is the eleventh-highest mountain in the world. Its name is often translated from Balti as 'beautiful mountain.'
climbing: Climbing requires a long glacier approach, expedition logistics and strong high-altitude experience. The region's weather and remoteness demand careful contingency planning.
facts: Gasherbrum I reaches 8,080 m.
It is also called Hidden Peak.
The first ascent in 1958 was made by an American team.

name: Annapurna I
intro: A sacred Himalayan massif whose name means 'full of food' in Sanskrit.
description: Annapurna I rises above central Nepal's deep valleys and is surrounded by a varied landscape of forests, villages and glaciers. The Annapurna region is one of the country's best-known trekking areas.
history: Maurice Herzog and Louis Lachenal reached the summit in 1950, making Annapurna I the first 8,000-metre peak climbed. The expedition was celebrated but came at a severe physical cost to the climbers.
geography: Annapurna I is 8,091 m high and is the tenth-highest mountain in the world. The Annapurna massif contains multiple major peaks and lies north of Pokhara.
climbing: The mountain's avalanche exposure makes a summit attempt highly serious. Trekkers can explore established routes in the surrounding region with local guides and proper altitude preparation.
facts: Annapurna I was the first 8,000-metre mountain to be climbed, in 1950.
The summit is 8,091 m high.
Annapurna Conservation Area is Nepal's largest protected area.

name: Matterhorn
intro: An instantly recognizable pyramid above Zermatt and the Italian Valtournenche.
description: The Matterhorn's four steep faces point toward the compass and straddle the Swiss–Italian border. Its silhouette rises over glaciers and alpine meadows, connecting the resort town of Zermatt with mountain villages in Italy.
history: Edward Whymper and his team made the first ascent in 1865 by the Hörnli Ridge. Four members died on the descent, a tragedy that became one of mountaineering's defining stories.
geography: The Matterhorn is part of the Pennine Alps and reaches 4,478 m. Its distinctive shape was formed by glacial erosion of hard rock.
climbing: The normal Hörnli route is a serious alpine climb, not a hiking trail. It requires excellent fitness, scrambling ability, suitable conditions and typically a qualified mountain guide.
facts: The summit is 4,478 m high.
The first ascent took place on 14 July 1865.
The Matterhorn straddles the Swiss–Italian border.

name: Mont Blanc
intro: Western Europe's highest mountain crowns a vast glacier-covered Alpine massif.
description: Mont Blanc rises among glaciers, aiguilles and deep valleys shared by France and Italy. Chamonix and Courmayeur are gateways to a region of historic climbing, high mountain huts and celebrated walking routes.
history: Jacques Balmat and Michel-Gabriel Paccard made the first recorded ascent in 1786, helping launch modern mountaineering. The summit's snow cap changes over time, so measured elevations vary with snow and survey conditions.
geography: Mont Blanc is the highest peak in the Alps. The summit lies in a border region whose precise national boundary is interpreted differently by France and Italy.
climbing: The normal Goûter route is a high-altitude alpine climb with rockfall and weather hazards. Reservations, current route conditions, acclimatization and qualified guidance are essential.
facts: A 2023 survey measured the summit at 4,805.59 m; snow conditions cause variation.
The first recorded ascent was in 1786.
The Tour du Mont Blanc is a multi-day trek around the massif, not a summit route.

name: Mount Elbrus
intro: A twin-coned dormant volcano in the Caucasus, often counted as Europe's highest summit.
description: Elbrus's snow-covered twin summits dominate the western Caucasus. The mountain is surrounded by alpine pastures, glaciers and the valleys of the Kabardino-Balkarian highlands.
history: The lower western summit was first climbed by an expedition led by the British mountaineer Douglas Freshfield in 1874. The eastern summit had been reached earlier, in 1829, by a local guide named Killar Khashirov.
geography: Elbrus is a dormant stratovolcano with two summits, the higher western top at 5,642 m. Its position in the Caucasus means definitions of the Europe–Asia boundary affect continental rankings.
climbing: The standard southern route uses lifts and high camps, but remains a serious high-altitude climb exposed to severe weather. Check current access, weather and local guidance before planning.
facts: The west summit is 5,642 m; the east summit is 5,621 m.
Elbrus is a dormant volcano.
The first ascent of the western summit was in 1874.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
intro: Africa's highest mountain rises as a solitary volcanic massif above the plains of Tanzania.
description: Kilimanjaro is a free-standing volcanic mountain with distinct ecological zones, from cultivated foothills and cloud forest to alpine desert and a glaciated summit. Its scale and isolation make it visible across the surrounding plains.
history: The first recorded summit ascent was made in 1889 by Hans Meyer, Ludwig Purtscheller and guide Yohani Kinyala Lauwo. The mountain and its surrounding habitats are protected within Kilimanjaro National Park.
geography: Kilimanjaro's highest point, Uhuru Peak, sits on Kibo, the tallest of three volcanic cones. The mountain reaches 5,895 m and is the highest point in Africa.
climbing: The summit is reached by non-technical trekking routes, but altitude sickness is a serious risk. Choose a longer itinerary for acclimatization, use licensed local operators and follow park rules.
facts: Uhuru Peak reaches 5,895 m.
Kilimanjaro has three volcanic cones: Kibo, Mawenzi and Shira.
Its routes pass through several distinct climate zones.

name: Mount Kenya
intro: An ancient volcanic mountain whose glacial peaks rise above central Kenya.
description: Mount Kenya is a dramatic extinct volcano of jagged rock towers, high moorland and unique Afro-alpine habitats. Forest and wildlife habitats ring the mountain, which is protected as a national park and UNESCO World Heritage site.
history: The first recorded ascent of Batian was made in 1899 by Halford Mackinder with guides César Ollier and Joseph Brocherel. The mountain's name and cultural importance are closely tied to the communities living around it.
geography: Batian, the highest point, reaches 5,199 m; Nelion is 5,188 m. These twin rocky summits are remnants of a much larger extinct volcano.
climbing: Point Lenana is a high trekking objective; Batian and Nelion require technical rock climbing. Conditions vary by route and season, so use local expertise and allow time for acclimatization.
facts: Batian is Kenya's highest point at 5,199 m.
Mount Kenya is an extinct volcano.
The protected area is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage site.

name: Denali
intro: North America's highest peak rises above the wilderness of Alaska.
description: Denali stands far above the surrounding Alaska Range, its great bulk often wrapped in fast-changing weather. Denali National Park preserves a vast landscape of tundra, glacial valleys and wildlife.
history: The mountain has long been known as Denali, 'the high one' in Koyukon Athabaskan. The first widely recognized ascent of the summit was completed in 1913 by Hudson Stuck, Harry Karstens, Walter Harper and Robert Tatum.
geography: Denali reaches 6,190 m and has the greatest vertical relief of any mountain above sea level. Its latitude contributes to exceptionally cold conditions and a lower effective atmospheric pressure than at comparable elevations closer to the equator.
climbing: The West Buttress is a long, cold, crevassed expedition route requiring glacier travel and self-sufficiency. Climbers must register in advance and follow National Park Service rules.
facts: Denali stands at 6,190 m.
Its name means 'the high one' in Koyukon.
The mountain is within Denali National Park and Preserve.

name: Mount Logan
intro: Canada's highest mountain is a vast, remote massif in the Yukon.
description: Mount Logan's broad, icy summit plateau contains numerous high points and rises above the Saint Elias Mountains. It is set in an immense wilderness of glaciers and icefields within Kluane National Park and Reserve.
history: The mountain was named for geologist Sir William Edmond Logan. A 1925 expedition made the first recorded ascent of the main summit, reaching it after a demanding journey across the ice.
geography: Mount Logan reaches 5,959 m and is the second-highest peak in North America. Its massive base and extensive glaciation make it one of the largest mountains by footprint.
climbing: The long approach and severe Arctic-influenced weather make Logan a major expedition. Climbers need glacier-travel expertise, self-sufficiency and a careful plan for remote rescue limitations.
facts: Mount Logan is Canada's highest point at 5,959 m.
It lies within the UNESCO-listed Kluane / Wrangell–St. Elias protected landscape.
Its broad summit plateau has several named subsidiary peaks.

name: Aconcagua
intro: The highest mountain outside Asia crowns the Andes of western Argentina.
description: Aconcagua rises above the dry, high valleys of Mendoza Province near the Chilean border. Its immense summit and glacial terrain are visible from a landscape of strikingly different desert and snow environments.
history: The first confirmed summit was reached in 1897 by Swiss climber Matthias Zurbriggen during an expedition led by Edward FitzGerald. The mountain lies within Aconcagua Provincial Park, where access is managed through permits.
geography: Aconcagua reaches 6,961 m and is the highest peak in both the Western and Southern Hemispheres. Though part of the Andes, it is not an active volcano.
climbing: The Normal Route is non-technical in good conditions but remains a demanding high-altitude expedition with serious weather and altitude risks. Permits, acclimatization and an experienced team are essential.
facts: Aconcagua is 6,961 m high.
It is the highest mountain outside Asia.
The Normal Route is a high-altitude trek rather than a technical climbing route in ordinary conditions.

name: Puncak Jaya
intro: A rare tropical glaciated summit rises from the forested highlands of western New Guinea.
description: Puncak Jaya, also known as Carstensz Pyramid, is the highest point of Indonesia and Oceania under the commonly used continental boundary. Its limestone walls rise above tropical rainforest, creating an extraordinary contrast of climates.
history: Dutch explorer and geologist Jan Carstensz reported seeing glaciers on the mountain in 1623, a claim that was initially met with skepticism. The first recorded ascent was made in 1962 by Heinrich Harrer and companions.
geography: The 4,884-metre summit is part of the Sudirman Range in the Central Highlands of Papua. Small equatorial glaciers have retreated dramatically in recent decades.
climbing: The commonly used route involves technical rock climbing and complex access in a remote region. Permits, local arrangements, experienced guides and current travel advice are essential.
facts: Puncak Jaya reaches 4,884 m.
It is the highest point in Indonesia and is often counted as Oceania's highest.
Its equatorial glaciers are among the few tropical glaciers on Earth and are rapidly shrinking.
